statusText: Green - weekend halt in force, Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt and no price path can form. headline: A 3.75%-4.00% policy rate, a 10-year near 5% and $100 crude sit out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash Nasdaq-100 settled Friday at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing near the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. The E-mini NQ last printed 29,917.25, up 0.59%, after opening at 29,723.75 and ranging 29,648.00-29,993.25. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 daily range. Friday was a quadruple-witching expiry, among the largest on record, and it cleared without disorder; the Nasdaq Composite closed 0.39% higher at 26,522.55. The week's anchor was Wednesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 vote raising the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase in more than three years, with a hawkish press conference and a dot plot pointing to at least one further hike in 2026. On decision day the Dow fell about 1.2% and the 10-year Treasury topped 5% for the first time since 2007; Thursday reversed much of it, with the Nasdaq Composite up 1.7% to 26,418.30. H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94% on 17 September, with effective fed funds at 3.88%. Front-month WTI settled at $100.30, down about 1.6%, and Brent at $103.87, down about 0.9%, a third consecutive decline as physical supply panic eased after Aramco signalled a partial East-West pipeline restart within days and full capacity in roughly six weeks; the outage put as much as 4m b/d of Hormuz-bypass capacity at risk and Strait of Hormuz shipping risk is unresolved. Friday's tape was dispersed rather than directional: megacaps split four up and four down for a mean change near +0.24%, with Broadcom up 2.97% against Meta down 2.43%, while semiconductors led on Arm +4.04%, Micron +3.92% and AMD +2.70% but with Qualcomm down 5.82%. Over the full week the Nasdaq gained about 0.7% while the S&P 500 slipped about 0.1% and the Dow fell 1.7%. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was only partially collected this cycle, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so futures and calendar evidence here rests on independently verified primary sources. Tail is held at its structural weekend floor because no price path can form: the pathological no-retracement structure that Tail measures has no venue in which to develop. Stress is low and drifts higher only as the stock of unpriced headlines grows against static marks. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the Sunday 22:00Z reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-19 through the European morning and the U.S. cash session, then fell to 11, 7, 6 and 5 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final six hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 27 into the halt, reaching 21 in the most recent slot. Confidence held between 80 and 88 throughout. Dominant mode rotated from trend-up in the European morning to mixed across the dispersed U.S. session, back briefly to trend-up into the close, then to normal once the weekend halt began.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about sixteen hours after the final slot here. Tail is held between 5 and 7 across the window, with a gradual lift through Saturday afternoon and the Sunday small hours that reflects the growing stock of unpriced headlines - principally the Hormuz supply file, the rates file after the hike, and AI policy into the 24 September Trump-Xi summit - rather than any observed structure. Stress rises slowly from 21 to 28 on the same reasoning, crossing into the moderate band during Saturday evening in Europe, and Confidence decays from 79 to 68 as Friday's verified marks age without a refreshing observation. Dominant mode is normal in every slot and the mapped policy state is unchanged throughout. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the reopen, where a gap that extends without a meaningful retracement alongside aligned yields, crude and semiconductors would be the structure that matters; a gap that is absorbed and retraced would be ordinary.
